sources.title: Shopify Delivers Big: 30%+ Growth Across GMV, Revenue, Gross Profit, and Free Cash Flow (Q2 2026)
Shopify Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025
AI commerce at scale (Universal Commerce Protocol announcement)
Commerce Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Results (press release as syndicated)
Lightspeed Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2026 Financial Results and Provides Outlook for Fiscal 2027

items.title: Payments are now the core monetization engine
items.summary: Shopify Payments processed 65.6% of GMV in FY2025 (61.9% in 2024) and 68% in Q2 2026; merchant solutions were 76% of FY2025 revenue.
items.implication: Checkout conversion, payment-method coverage and payout trust drive platform economics more than plan pricing; payments bricks are tier-one investments.

items.title: Platform GMV is compounding at about 30% a year
items.summary: GMV reached $378.4bn in FY2025 (+29%) and $115.6bn in Q2 2026 (+32%).
items.implication: Scale effects (network risk data, saved-buyer reach, catalog breadth) strengthen with GMV and favor the leader in replatforming decisions.

items.title: Subscription revenue grows slower than merchant solutions
items.summary: MRR was $205m at end of 2025 (+15%) and $221m in Q2 2026 (+20%) while merchant solutions grew 35% in FY2025.
items.implication: Small-merchant success should be measured by survival and solution attach, not plan revenue alone.

items.title: AI assistants are becoming a sales channel with merchants enabled by default
items.summary: The Universal Commerce Protocol, co-developed with Google, lets agents handle discovery to checkout using merchant checkout rules; merchants are enabled by default. Shopify claims Catalog-powered AI searches convert at 2x those using scraped data.
items.implication: Structured catalog quality and agent checkout reliability become conversion levers equal to the storefront; merchants need per-channel control and reporting.

items.title: The saved-buyer wallet extends beyond the platform's own merchants
items.summary: Shopify's Spring '26 Edition cites 250M+ Shop Pay shoppers and opens Shop Pay to brands not on Shopify, plus sign-in with Shop for developers.
items.implication: Buyer identity is a network asset; growing it off-platform raises recognition rates on-platform.

items.title: The app ecosystem is large and moving into the AI assistant
items.summary: More than 21,000 apps are listed (FY2025 10-K); Sidekick app extensions launched with 15+ partners including Klaviyo, Loop and Smile.
items.implication: Partner economics now depend on assistant exposure as well as app store ranking; extension contracts must be stable.

items.title: Merchant base is international but still US-weighted
items.summary: Merchants come from more than 175 countries: 44% United States, 31% EMEA, 16% APAC/China, 5% Canada, 5% Latin America (FY2025 10-K).
items.implication: Markets, duties and local payment methods are growth levers; cross-border features must work for US-based brands selling abroad and vice versa.

items.title: Open SaaS challenger growth has stalled
items.summary: Commerce.com (formerly BigCommerce) reported FY2025 revenue of $342.3m (+3%) and net revenue retention of 95.2%.
items.implication: Replatforming flows favor the leader; win-rate and migration cycle time are the competitive KPIs for premium merchants.

items.title: POS specialists are growing payments in retail and hospitality
items.summary: Lightspeed reported Q4 FY2026 GPV of $9.6bn (+22%) and about 150,000 customer locations, focusing on North American retail and European hospitality.
items.implication: Enterprise POS wins depend on in-person payments, hardware and vertical depth, not only on shared online-offline data.

items.title: Lending grows with balance-sheet risk
items.summary: In FY2025 loans and merchant cash advances (net) increased by $560m and lending-related losses rose by $61m (FY2025 10-K).
items.implication: Capital is a retention and growth lever for small merchants but needs underwriting tied to live sales and loss monitoring.
